'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]]
***[[Rafah offensive]]
****The [[Israel Defense Forces]] retakes control of [[Rafah]], prompting thousands of [[Palestinians]] to flee the city. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/hundreds-thousands-flee-israel-seizes-rafah-new-gaza-security-zone-2025-04-03/ (Reuters)]
****At least 100 [[Palestinians]] are killed and 70 others are injured, including some critically, in [[airstrike]]s across the [[Gaza Strip]]. One of the strikes killed at least 27 people, including 8 men, 14 women, and 5 children, at a sheltering school in the north. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-gaza-hamas-strike-casualties-76c88384839a9ac71c87f0045278c385 (AP News)]
*[[M23 campaign (2022–present)|M23 campaign]]
**[[2025 Walikale offensive]]
***[[March 23 Movement|M23]] spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka claims that the group's withdrawal from [[Walikale]], [[North Kivu Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], was to show goodwill for [[peace negotiations]]. [https://www.criticalthreats.org/briefs/congo-war-security-review/congo-war-security-review-april-3-2025#_edn5a8850a81da37df564dcd4df35bbe9211 (Critical Threats)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**At least five [[Jalisco New Generation Cartel|CJNG]] gunmen are killed and 116 explosive devices seized after a combined operation that took place in [[Apatzingán]]. In the same day, in the municipality of [[Parácuaro]], an encounter between delinquents, the [[Secretariat of National Defense|SEDENA]] and the [[National Guard (Mexico)|National Guard]] leaves one gunman killed. [https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2025/04/03/estados/abate-el-ejercito-a-cinco-pistoleros-en-apatzingan (''La Jornada'')] [https://www.contramuro.com/gatillero-abatido-enfrentamiento-paracuaro/ (Contramuro)]
*A dispute between two groups of [[miner]]s over access to [[gold|gold deposits]] in [[La Paz Department (Bolivia)|La Paz Department]], [[Bolivia]], escalates into clashes with six people reportedly killed and several others missing. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/bolivia-wildcat-mining-clash-sees-explosions-six-reported-dead-2025-04-03/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Tariffs in the second Trump administration]]
**A 25% [[tariff]] on all [[automotive industry|automotive]] imports into the [[United States]] enters force. No exemptions are announced despite requests from several [[List of countries by leading trade partners|major trade partners]], including [[Japan]] and the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-25-automobile-tariffs-due-take-effect-1201-am-et-april-3-federal-register-2025-04-02/ (Reuters)]
**[[Multinational corporation|Multinational]] [[Automotive industry|car manufacturer]] [[Stellantis]] announces it will [[layoff|lay off]] 900 workers across five of its U.S. factories and will pause production at assembly plants in [[Canada]] and [[Mexico]] in response to the tariffs. [https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/stellantis-says-will-temporarily-lay-off-900-us-workers-following-tariff-2025-04-03/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[January 2025 Southern California wildfires]]
**The death toll from [[wildfire]]s in [[Southern California]], U.S., increases to 30. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/article/death-toll-from-the-wildfires-that-tore-through-the-los-angeles-area-reaches-30/ (CTV News)]
*[[Mediterranean Sea migrant smuggling]]
**Two boats carrying [[Illegal immigration|migrants]] capsize in the early hours of the morning near [[Lesbos]] in the [[Aegean Sea]], killing 16 people and leaving one more missing. More than 40 people are rescued by the [[Hellenic Coast Guard]]. [https://apnews.com/article/migration-greece-capsize-lesbos-f8b58302de27e3a819b0bad02b32b28f (AP)]
*[[Tornado outbreak of April 1–3, 2025]]
**At least seven people are killed and thirteen others are injured by overnight severe weather including [[tornado]]es, [[storm]]s, [[hail]] and [[flood]]s across [[Tennessee]], [[Missouri]], and [[Indiana]] in the [[United States]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/weather/floods/live-blog/severe-weather-live-updates-life-threatening-catastrophic-flash-floodi-rcna199446 (NBC News)]
*Eight people are killed after an [[Antonov An-12]] crashes near [[El Fasher]], [[Sudan]]. [https://aviation-safety.net/wikibase/509084 (Aviation Safety Network)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Hungary–Israel relations]]
**[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] lands in [[Budapest|Budapest, Hungary]], a signatory of the [[International Criminal Court]] (ICC), for a state visit in defiance of the [[International Criminal Court arrest warrants for Israeli leaders|international arrest warrant]] against him for alleged [[war crime]]s. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/article-848634 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] [https://apnews.com/article/netanyahu-visits-hungary-despite-international-arrest-warrant-d3ce4f986adbff6c324b8ef86261731e (AP)]
**The [[Government of Hungary|Hungarian government]] announces it will withdraw from the ICC. [https://www.reuters.com/world/hungary-says-it-is-withdrawing-icc-israeli-leader-visits-2025-04-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[China]] arrests three [[Filipinos]] suspected of espionage near Chinese military facilities as part of a network recruited by Philippine intelligence to gather sensitive information. The Philippines say the arrests are related to previous [[2025 China–Philippine espionage cases|arrests]] of Chinese nationals for similar offences. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/east-asia/china-arrests-filipinos-suspected-spying-5041696 (AFP via CNA)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/philippines-alarmed-over-china-arrest-alleged-filipino-spies-2025-04-05/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025 Turkish protests]]
**[[General Directorate of Security (Turkey)|Turkish National Police]] detain eleven people for spreading calls for and participating in shopping [[boycott]]s in [[Turkey|the country]] as a protest against the [[Arrest of Ekrem İmamoğlu|arrest]] of [[Istanbul]] [[Mayor of Istanbul|mayor]] and opposition [[Next Turkish presidential election|presidential candidate]] [[Ekrem İmamoğlu]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/turkey-detains-11-people-for-pro-government-business-boycott-calls/a-72124660 (DW)]
*[[Canada convoy protests]]
**The [[Ontario Court of Justice]] in [[Ontario]], [[Canada]], convicts [[Tamara Lich]] and [[Christopher John Barber|Chris Barber]], two leaders of the [[truck driver]] protest movement against [[COVID-19 vaccination in Canada]], of [[mischief|criminal mischief]]. [https://apnews.com/article/canada-trucker-protests-organizers-guilty-a45b9c16148a1453f290b86350fea795 (AP)]
*[[Mass shootings in the United States]]
**Three people, including the perpetrator, are killed and two others are injured in a [[mass shooting]] when a 29-year-old man shoots his mother and at passing cars in [[Sabattus, Maine|Sabattus]], [[Maine]], United States. [https://www.wmtw.com/article/sabattus-maine-deadly-shooting-man-kills-mother-passerby/64378039 (ABC News)]
*Seven people,  including the perpetrator, are injured in a [[mass stabbing]] near [[Gallaudet University]] in [[Washington, D.C.]], United States. A suspect was arrested. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/crime/washington-dc-stabbing-injuries-b2727099.html (''The Independent'')]
*A 50-year-old man [[Self-immolation|sets himself on fire]] inside of his car in a failed [[car bomb]]ing near the [[National Monument (Amsterdam)|National Monument]] on [[Dam Square]] in [[Amsterdam]], [[Netherlands]], causing a small explosion and injuring himself. No bystanders were injured. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/video-moment-car-exploded-in-iconic-amsterdam-square-8079954 (NDTV)]
